meta.title: Assessment of knowledge, Attitude and Practice regarding Periodontal health among IT Professionals in Bangalore City- a cross sectional questionnaire survey

hero.summary: This report keeps Bangalore at the center of the analysis without discarding the outside-Bangalore respondents who also contributed useful signal.
executive_bullets: Bangalore drives the dataset, but the city is not a single cluster.
Named Bangalore localities differ more in behavior than in awareness.
Ulsoor stands out as a small pocket where knowledge is not turning into routine practice.
The weakest knowledge area is not advanced care; it is the basic cause of gum disease.
Daily routines weaken most on interdental cleaning and dentist follow-up.

sections.summary: The lowest-scoring knowledge items concern the primary cause of gum disease and the definitions of plaque and tartar.

insights.title: Bangalore drives the dataset, but the city is not a single cluster.
insights.summary: The report should treat Bangalore as the main lens while still showing that responses come from several visible Bengaluru pockets.
evidence: Bangalore contributes 146 of 251 responses (58.2%).
JP Nagar is the largest named Bangalore locality with 12 responses.
Bellandur, Whitefield, and HSR Layout each contribute meaningful local pockets of responses.
insights.why_it_matters: Presentation should not talk about Bangalore as if it were one homogeneous block; locality cuts are needed for a credible city-specific story.

insights.title: Named Bangalore localities differ more in behavior than in awareness.
insights.summary: Practice is strongest in a few named Bangalore pockets even when knowledge stays closer to the city average.
evidence: Whitefield posts the highest reported practice score among claimable Bangalore localities at 80.0%.
JP Nagar and HSR Layout also clear 75% on practice.
The Bangalore-wide practice mean is 70.9%.
insights.why_it_matters: Locality messaging can highlight where good routines already exist and use those pockets as proof that stronger behavior is achievable inside the same city context.

insights.title: Ulsoor stands out as a small pocket where knowledge is not turning into routine practice.
insights.summary: The biggest knowledge-to-behavior mismatch inside Bangalore appears in a locality-sized pocket, not in the city average.
evidence: Ulsoor records 92.0% on knowledge and 55.3% on practice.
That creates a 36.7-point knowledge-practice gap.
This comparison is based on 5 respondents, so it should be presented as a directional pocket rather than a citywide conclusion.
insights.why_it_matters: This is the clearest example that awareness alone does not guarantee daily action, which points toward behavior-focused interventions rather than awareness messaging alone.

chart.caption: Ulsoor has the largest knowledge-practice gap among localities with at least five respondents.

insights.title: The weakest knowledge area is not advanced care; it is the basic cause of gum disease.
insights.summary: The biggest misconception sits at the foundation of periodontal understanding, which makes it especially important for public messaging.
evidence: Only 37.5% answered the early gum disease cause question correctly.
Plaque and tartar questions also stay near the halfway mark at 51.4% and 51.4%.
The overall knowledge average is 63.6%.
insights.why_it_matters: If the basics are still unclear, communication should start with plain explanations of plaque, tartar, and disease causation before moving to treatment messaging.

insights.title: Daily routines weaken most on interdental cleaning and dentist follow-up.
insights.summary: The weakest behaviors are not brushing basics alone; they are the routines people skip once a toothbrush is no longer enough.
evidence: Only 12.0% land in the best-practice band for cleaning aids.
Dental visit recency reaches only 39.0% best-practice adherence.
Half or more of respondents remain in the low-quality bands for brushing direction and dentist visits.
insights.why_it_matters: This points to a concrete behavior agenda: move beyond brushing frequency and focus on interdental cleaning and regular dental follow-up.

insights.title: Bangalore respondents are more attitude-positive, but knowledge and behavior look broadly similar to the outside-Bangalore sample.
insights.summary: The geography story is more about attitude tone than about a dramatic difference in knowledge or practice.
evidence: Bangalore averages 69.6% on attitude versus 66.1% outside Bangalore.
The attitude gap is 3.5 points with a small effect size of 0.190.
Knowledge and practice differences are directionally smaller than the attitude split.
insights.why_it_matters: Outside-Bangalore respondents still belong in the story because the differences are not large enough to dismiss them as a separate population.

chart.subtitle: Mean standardized scores by geo scope.
chart.caption: Attitude shows the clearest Bangalore-versus-outside contrast, while knowledge and practice stay closer together.

insights.title: Knowledge aligns most strongly with practice, more than with attitude alone.
insights.summary: Among the three composite domains, the cleanest statistical relationship is between knowing more and reporting better routines.
evidence: Knowledge vs Practice has the strongest Spearman rho at 0.381.
The 95% bootstrap interval runs from 0.264 to 0.491.
Attitude also matters, but the practice link is weaker when attitude is paired with practice directly.
insights.why_it_matters: This connects awareness-building with behavior change, while still acknowledging that knowledge alone is not sufficient in every locality or segment.

chart.title: Relationships among knowledge, attitude, and practice
chart.subtitle: Darker circles represent stronger monotonic relationships.
chart.caption: Knowledge shows its strongest alignment with practice at rho=0.381.

insights.title: The weakest reported practice is concentrated in a few work and career segments, not across the whole sample.
insights.summary: Behavior challenges are concentrated enough to support more targeted messaging instead of a single blanket intervention.
evidence: Work from home (Remote) has the lowest practice score among segments with at least 10 respondents at 66.5%.
10-15 years follows close behind at 66.8%.
0-3 years rounds out the bottom three practice segments.
insights.why_it_matters: This makes the case for segment-aware outreach, especially when presenting recommendations to workplace or community stakeholders.

method_notes: Knowledge, attitude, and practice scores are recomputed directly from the raw item responses in the source CSV.
Bangalore-specific locality analysis preserves named Bengaluru localities whenever a locality reaches at least three responses; smaller pockets roll into Other Bangalore localities.
Locality-level claims are only elevated when a Bangalore locality reaches at least five responses.
Subgroup comparisons use non-parametric tests, and the regression appendix is included only as a supporting validation layer.
appendix.mapping_review_head: A reviewed locality-mapping table is written alongside the report data for inspection.
